name: Can a pool remodel improve drainage around the backyard?

mainEntity.name: Can a pool remodel improve drainage around the backyard?
mainEntity.text: Can a pool remodel improve drainage around the backyard?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pool remodel can improve drainage, but only if drainage is included in the scope. Many backyard drainage problems come from the deck, grading, or hardscape around the pool rather than the shell itself. During a remodel, contractors can correct slopes, add drains, improve runoff paths, and rebuild areas that cause standing water. This is especially important in Los Angeles properties with tight side yards, sloped lots, or older decks that have settled over time. Poor drainage can lead to slippery surfaces, staining, erosion, and repeated damage to coping or plaster. If the backyard already puddles after rain or irrigation, a pool-only refresh will not solve the root problem. Homeowners should ask whether the remodel includes drainage evaluation and whether any deck repairs will change the finished slope. A good scope should explain how water will move away from the pool and house. Addressing drainage at the same time as the remodel usually produces a more durable result.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a pool remodel can improve drainage if the plan includes regrading, deck replacement, drainage channels, and proper runoff control. Drainage problems are often tied to the pool deck and surrounding hardscape rather than the pool shell itself. Fixing only the pool surface will not correct backyard flooding.
